notes: Evals for the task-spec skill (v3.4). Each prompt is what a real user/agent would say to invoke Task-Spec authoring. Expectations verify the crown jewels: the 6 zones, the behavior-to-eval traceability chain, runnable bash evals (the moat), the SIX-TIER effort gate (XS/S/M/L leaves run; XL/XXL nodes decompose into children — no route out to SDD), the closed loop (validate -> safe-to-delegate), and vendor-neutral frontmatter. Prompts 1-4 are authoring cases; 5 tests XL/XXL DECOMPOSITION (not refusal); 6 tests legacy conversion. Grounded in this repo's postgres->duckdb->dbt->MCP stack where a codebase is needed.

evals.prompt: Create a task-spec to add a dbt gold model gold_daily_revenue_by_category over the landed raw.* tables in the DuckDB warehouse. Revenue = SUM(payments.amount) where status='captured', grouped by product category and UTC order date.
evals.expected_output: A T-*.md Task-Spec file with all 6 zones, a Behavior section (Given/When/Then, B-N ids), at least 3 runnable bash evals each carrying verifies:[B-N], a validation_card, and an Exit Check that calls every eval. Frontmatter names a valid leaf tier (this one is S or M), touches_paths within the tier budget, and format_version 3.
expectations: The output creates a T-*.md file under a tasks/ directory
The file contains a '## Behavior' section with at least one Given/When/Then clause using a B-N identifier
The file contains at least 3 bash eval functions (eval_1, eval_2, eval_3 or more)
Each behavior B-N is referenced by at least one eval's verifies: field (behavior-to-eval traceability)
The file contains an Exit Check that invokes every eval_N defined
The frontmatter declares format_version: 3 (or profile standard/full) and a valid leaf effort class (XS/S/M/L; here S or M) within the tier write-surface budget
The output does NOT hardcode 'paid' as the payment status (the real status is 'captured')

evals.prompt: Turn this meeting note into a task-spec: 'We agreed the MCP query tool should return daily revenue by category, reading only the gold table, never raw. Ship it this sprint.'
evals.expected_output: A single atomic Task-Spec whose source_note records the meeting-note provenance, with a do-not-touch/anti-patterns zone that forbids reading raw.* (serving reads gold only), behaviors traced to evals, and a runnable eval that calls the MCP tool and checks its result matches the gold query.
expectations: The frontmatter includes a source_note field referencing the meeting-note provenance
The Guardrails/anti-patterns or do-not-touch zone forbids reading raw.* (serving reads gold only)
At least one eval verifies the tool's output equals the gold-table source of truth
Every declared behavior maps to at least one eval and vice versa

evals.prompt: Author a lite-profile task-spec for a one-line docs fix: update the README to reference cvg-aut-systems-spine-steps-v2.pdf instead of v1.
evals.expected_output: A lite-profile Task-Spec: Intent + at least one runnable eval, with the Behavior section optional (lite allows omitting it). Effort S. The eval greps the README for the new filename and asserts the old one is gone.
expectations: The frontmatter sets profile: lite
The task carries at least one runnable bash eval
The eval objectively checks the README content (presence of the new filename and/or absence of the old)
Effort is classified S

evals.prompt: I need a task-spec that any engine (Claude, Codex, or Cursor) can pick up and run unattended to build the silver_orders dbt model. Make it vendor-neutral.
evals.expected_output: A Task-Spec with execution_backend: any (open string), an agent_contract block (produce/emit/required_tools/timeout_minutes/sandbox_type), and evals that gate on dbt build + schema tests. No vendor-specific field names.
expectations: The frontmatter sets execution_backend: any (or an open-string token, not a closed enum)
The file contains an agent_contract block with required_tools, emit, and timeout_minutes
No vendor-named metadata fields like codex_metadata or kimi_metadata appear (backend_metadata is the generic key if any)
The evals are runnable bash tied to dbt build / schema tests

evals.prompt: Create a task-spec to migrate our entire analytics platform from Postgres to Snowflake, including re-architecting all pipelines and the serving layer. It's a multi-week effort.
evals.expected_output: The skill classifies this as an XXL decomposition NODE and DECOMPOSES it — never routing out to SDD. It produces a parent node Task-Spec with effort: XXL and a children: block (>=3 child task-spec ids), and the children are runnable leaf atoms (XS/S/M/L) sliced along the natural seams (e.g. per pipeline / per layer). The node owns no write surface (touches_paths: []); a worker dispatches the children, and safe-to-delegate refuses to delegate the node directly.
expectations: The skill does NOT produce a single runnable Task-Spec for this multi-week request, and does NOT route to SDD/AgentSpec (that path is retired)
The response identifies the work as an XL/XXL decomposition NODE
The response DECOMPOSES into child task-specs: a parent node (effort XL/XXL, touches_paths: [], a children: list) plus runnable leaf atoms (XS/S/M/L) sliced along seams
It notes the node itself is not delegated — a worker runs the leaves and composes their results back up

evals.prompt: Convert this legacy markdown checklist task into a proper task-spec: '- [ ] add health endpoint\n- [ ] write test\n- [ ] update docs'.
evals.expected_output: A migrated Task-Spec where each checklist item becomes a runnable eval (or is folded into the Behavior + evals), with the legacy content preserved and format_version set. Uses migrate-legacy-task.sh semantics.
expectations: Each checklist item is turned into a runnable eval or a traced behavior, not left as prose checkboxes
The output is a well-formed Task-Spec with the 6 zones and an Exit Check
The migration preserves the original intent (health endpoint + test + docs)
